name: Alex Applicant

education_history.thesis_title: Planning and Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

projects.title: Autonomous Agents for Software Engineering
projects.description: Built a multi-agent framework using Gemini, LangGraph and MCP for automatic GitHub issue triage, debugging and pull-request generation. The system used planning, tool use, memory and reflection loops.

projects.title: Evaluating LLM Hallucinations
projects.description: Developed a benchmark and evaluation metric for measuring hallucination rates in instruction-tuned language models. Compared GPT, Gemini and open-source models.

projects.title: Multi-Agent Research Assistant
projects.description: Built an agent system that performs literature review, paper summarization and citation tracing using OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar.

intro_call_summary: Alex wants to pursue a research-focused PhD working on robust agentic systems, AI alignment and long-horizon reasoning. They are particularly interested in planning, memory, tool use and coordination between multiple AI agents. Alex prefers professors with strong publication records in LLM reasoning, multi-agent systems and safety. They want programs with strong industry collaboration and funded PhD opportunities. They are open to interdisciplinary work involving reinforcement learning, interpretability and trustworthy AI.
raw_resume_text: Alex Applicant is a research-oriented MSc Computer Science student with interests in agentic AI, LLM reasoning, AI safety and alignment. During a research internship at AI Lab, Alex worked on autonomous software engineering agents capable of planning and executing multi-step tasks across GitHub repositories. Their work involved LangGraph, MCP, retrieval-augmented generation, memory systems and evaluation pipelines. Alex has experience training transformer models using PyTorch and has conducted experiments on hallucination reduction, tool-use optimization and agent planning. They have published survey work on LLM agents and are interested in pursuing doctoral research focused on scalable oversight, alignment, multi-agent coordination, planning under uncertainty and trustworthy autonomous systems.
